review_candidates.title: VP, Financial Controller - PE-backed Fiber Network Provider
review_candidates.description: Position : Vice President, Controller Reports to : Chief Financial Officer Location : Fully remote (United States) Travel : Minimal; approximately one to two trips per year, no more than quarterly Duration & Type : Full-Time, Monday - Friday; Fully REMOTE Company : A Rapidly Growing, Private Equity backed Fiber Network Provider Compensation : Competitive base salary and year-end performance bonus. Total rewards include healthcare (medical, dental, vision), PTO policy, paid holidays, 401(k), and additional rewards. Chamberlain Advisors is seeking an assertive, hands-on, and strategic Vice President, Controller to join a rapidly growing, private equity backed fiber-to-the-home internet service provider. This is a high-impact leadership role for an execution-oriented accounting leader who brings strong GAAP fundamentals, operational rigor, and the confidence to take full command of the accounting and treasury functions. As a key partner to the CFO, you will own the close, the balance sheet, Capex and construction-in-process (CIP) reporting, cash management, and lender and covenant reporting, while supporting an active inorganic growth strategy that includes tuck-in acquisitions and an expanded credit facility. We are looking for a results-oriented leader who sets a high standard, holds a team accountable, and thrives in a lean, direct, and fast-moving environment. This role offers the opportunity to shape the financial foundation of a company in a period of exceptional growth and to play a meaningful role in its next stage of scale. Summary Of Most Suitable Profile The most suitable candidate is an assertive, process-driven controller-level leader with strong GAAP fundamentals and a track record of owning the full accounting function in fast-growing, Capex-intensive environments such as fiber, telecom, broadband, cable, or telecom-adjacent construction. They are a strategist and team leader, not a bookkeeper: they take control of the close, set clear expectations, deliver direct feedback, and make difficult people decisions when the business requires it. They bring proven ERP ownership (NetSuite preferred), deep command of CIP/Capex accounting, and hands-on experience with treasury and cash management, lender reporting and covenant compliance, audit delivery, and acquisition accounting including purchase price allocation (PPA) and integration. Ultimately, they are a builder and an execution force who is energized by a direct, results-first leadership culture and ready to raise the bar for an accounting team in transition. Core profile: alignment with one of these two core profiles is required to get you in the conversation An Experienced Controller or VP, Controller for a High-Growth, PE-Backed, Capex-Intensive Business: A seasoned accounting leader who has owned the full accounting function, including close, balance sheet integrity, external audit, and lender and covenant reporting, in a private equity backed, asset-heavy environment. Brings strong Capex/CIP accounting expertise, ideally from fiber, broadband, telecom infrastructure, or similarly project-based industries, along with treasury and cash management responsibility. Has supported acquisitions, debt financings, or refinancings and is comfortable operating at the pace those events demand. A decisive, assertive leader who has elevated teams, including remote staff, and is willing to address underperformance directly. A Proven Corporate Controller Ready to Step Into a VP-Level Seat: A high-performing corporate controller in a rapidly scaling organization who has owned the month-end close, financial statements, and audit, and is ready to take on expanded scope across treasury, M&A accounting, and debt reporting. Brings a strong command of ISP/broadband, telecom, or capital-intensive accounting, has leveraged an ERP to strengthen reporting and controls, and has had exposure to acquisitions (diligence support, PPA, integration) and credit facility reporting. Combines hands-on execution with strategic thinking, and is motivated by the opportunity to lead a team through a period of transformation while partnering closely with a hands-on CFO. Differentiators: these will set you apart in the selection process Assertive, Results-Oriented Leadership Presence: The ideal candidate takes control of the function from day one. They are comfortable in a direct, high-accountability culture where feedback is candid and results come first. They speak up, advocate for their ideas, set clear standards, and hold their team to them. They have made difficult personnel decisions, including exiting underperformers, and understand that acting decisively when the business requires it is a core responsibility of leadership. This is not a role for a gentle player-coach; it is a role for a confident leader who raises the bar and expects others to meet it. Execution Force Through Complex, Concurrent Events: The strongest candidates have delivered BAU close and reporting while simultaneously supporting events such as acquisitions, purchase price allocations, debt upsizing or refinancing, and an annual audit. They prioritize ruthlessly, triage balance sheet issues quickly, and keep multiple workstreams moving without sacrificing accuracy. They are energized by a lean environment with significant short-term demands and bring the stamina and organization to execute through it. GAAP Foundation and Technical Accounting Acumen: The optimal candidate brings CPA-level accounting mastery with a strong command of core accounting fundamentals, including disciplined month-end close processes, thorough balance sheet reconciliations, and unwavering GAAP compliance. They must be able to identify and remediate non-GAAP practices, such as missing accruals or prepaids, incorrect revenue recognition, improper capitalization, or unamortized commissions. Competency with key standards, including ASC 805 (business combinations and PPA), ASC 606, ASC 842, debt modifications or extinguishments, and deferred financing fee amortization, is essential. While this role does not require a deep technical specialist, the controller must confidently flag technical issues, diagnose root causes, and drive the appropriate corrective actions. Treasury, Debt, and Covenant Discipline: The company does not have a separate treasury function, so this leader will own cash management, cash forecasting, and liquidity visibility. The ideal candidate has prepared accurate lender reporting and covenant compliance calculations, understands borrowing base and capacity considerations, and has worked alongside a CFO through a credit facility amendment, upsize, or new lead lender process. Precision here is non-negotiable; accurate covenant reporting is a defining expectation of the role. Capex, CIP, and Telecom-Adjacent Accounting Experience: The desired candidate brings strong experience in capital-intensive, infrastructure-heavy environments where Capex and CIP accounting is critical. They must be adept at tracking and reporting CIP, managing the full project life cycle from construction through in-service and depreciation, and allocating spend between key drivers such as new passings and new subscribers. Experience within telecom, fiber, wireline, cable, or closely related construction-based industries is strongly preferred. Financial Reporting, Data Integrity, and ERP Optimization: The strongest candidates produce accurate, insight-rich financial reporting built on uncompromising data integrity and disciplined system controls. They deliver clear, timely financial statements supported by high-quality close packages and meaningful variance commentary. They bring strong ownership of mid-market ERP systems, NetSuite preferred, with hands-on experience configuring the GL, maintaining the chart of accounts, and maximizing out-of-the-box reporting tools, and they can integrate acquired entities onto the platform efficiently. Strategic Thinking and Ability to Go Beyond the Numbers: The model candidate is a strategist, not a bookkeeper. They interpret results, identify trends, risks, and operational drivers, and translate data into clear "what this means" narratives for the CFO, lenders, and the board. They spot issues early, see around corners, and proactively surface opportunities or concerns that impact financial and operational performance. People Leadership and Ability to Elevate a Remote Team: The ideal candidate is a strong, hands-on people leader who sets high expectations and builds a team capable of meeting them. They bring the confidence to hold others accountable, address performance gaps promptly, and make talent decisions that strengthen the function. With proven success managing remote or distributed teams, this leader builds structure, clarity, and a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement. What You Will Be Accountable For Accomplishing Lead and Strengthen the Accounting Function Take full ownership of a disciplined, GAAP-compliant month-end close, driving accuracy, timeliness, and a long-term close target of approximately 5 business days. Triage and remediate balance sheet issues, ensuring all accounts are fully reconciled, supported, and audit-ready. Build, refine, and enforce best-practice processes across reconciliations, accruals, prepaids, revenue recognition, capitalization rules, and other core accounting activities. Identify and remediate any remaining non-GAAP policies, e.g., incorrect revenue recognition, missing accruals, lack of prepaids, improper capitalization, and unamortized commissions. Treasury, Cash Management, and Debt Reporting Own the treasury function, including daily cash management, cash forecasting, banking relationships, and liquidity visibility. Support the CFO through the credit facility upsize and new lead lender process, including data requests, compliance certificates, and reporting deliverables. Proactively flag liquidity considerations, covenant risks, or borrowing capacity issues. M&A Accounting and Integration Support due diligence on acquisition targets, including quality of financial information, balance sheet review, and accounting policy alignment. Own acquisition accounting, including purchase price allocation (PPA), opening balance sheets, and related ASC 805 considerations, in coordination with outside advisors. Integrate acquired businesses into the company's close process, chart of accounts, ERP, and control environment. Build a repeatable integration playbook to support an ongoing buy-and-build strategy. Audit and External Reporting Lead the annual audit and financial statement issuance, serving as the primary point of contact for external auditors. Maintain audit-ready documentation, technical accounting memos, and a strong internal control environment. Capex / CIP Accounting Ownership Lead CIP tracking and reporting across the full project life cycle, from construction to in-service to depreciation. Maintain accurate cost accumulation at the project level and translate results into high-level reporting for executives and investors (e.g., allocation between new passings and new subscribers). Partner closely with the Director of Cost Accounting to ensure accurate Capex accounting and alignment with grant or regulatory requirements. Accounting Operations and ERP Ownership (NetSuite Preferred) Assess and modernize accounting operations workflows, including AP, invoice processing, cash application, and vendor management, moving from manual processes to automated, scalable ones. Serve as the functional owner of the ERP environment, including GL configuration, chart-of-accounts structure, module setup, and reporting tools. Improve system utilization to support a faster close, stronger internal controls, and scalable reporting without requiring IT or external consultants for basic enhancements. Financial Reporting and Analysis Produce accurate monthly financial statements, close packages, and variance analysis with clear narratives on trends, risks, anomalies, and operational insights. Support board, investor, and lender reporting with high-quality analysis that goes beyond simply delivering numbers. Partner with the CFO and Director of FP&A on budgeting, forecasting, and operational reporting. People Leadership and Team Elevation Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team that includes general ledger accountants, AP staff, and a cost accounting function. What Qualifications You Will Need Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field required. Progressive accounting experience including leadership of the full accounting function as a Controller or Corporate Controller. review_candidates.description: Job Title: Senior District Cooling Energy Optimization Specialist Location: United Arab Emirates (Remote) Employment Type: Full-Time Work Arrangement: 100% Remote — Work From Home Level: Senior About the Role We are seeking an experienced Senior District Cooling Energy Optimization Specialist to analyze and improve the energy efficiency, operational performance, and cost effectiveness of district cooling systems. This role focuses on evaluating cooling plant performance, chilled water distribution efficiency, energy consumption patterns, equipment operating parameters, and thermal load profiles to identify opportunities for optimization. The successful candidate will use operational data, engineering analysis, performance dashboards, and remote monitoring platforms to recommend improvements to plant efficiency and network performance. Working entirely remotely, the specialist will collaborate with plant operators, facilities teams, engineering consultants, and energy management stakeholders. The role requires strong technical knowledge of chilled water systems, thermal energy performance, and energy optimization methodologies. Key Responsibilities Lead remote energy performance analysis and optimization initiatives for district cooling plants and distribution networks. Analyze plant operating data, including cooling capacity, electricity consumption, chilled water supply and return temperatures, and system flow rates. Monitor and evaluate key performance indicators such as coefficient of performance (COP), kW per refrigeration ton (kW/RT), plant efficiency, and overall system energy intensity. Assess chiller performance and identify opportunities to improve sequencing, loading, staging, and operating efficiency. Review chilled water distribution performance, including differential pressure, flow balance, temperature differential, and pumping energy consumption. Analyze cooling demand profiles and develop load forecasting models to support efficient plant operation and capacity planning. Evaluate the energy performance of chillers, cooling towers, pumps, heat exchangers, and associated auxiliary equipment using available operational data. Identify inefficient operating conditions, excessive energy consumption, abnormal temperature differentials, and potential equipment performance deterioration. Recommend optimization strategies involving variable-speed drives, pump control, chilled water temperature reset, condenser water optimization, and equipment scheduling. Review building interface performance and investigate issues associated with energy transfer, secondary-side flow, and cooling demand variation. Assess thermal energy meter data and identify inconsistencies affecting consumption analysis, billing support, or performance reporting. Develop energy models, baseline assessments, and performance comparisons to quantify potential efficiency improvements. Prepare technical reports detailing energy savings opportunities, optimization recommendations, expected operational benefits, and implementation considerations. Support remote monitoring and analytics initiatives using building management systems (BMS), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), and energy management platforms. Collaborate with plant operations teams to review optimization proposals and evaluate implementation results using verified performance data. Analyze historical trends to identify seasonal variations, unusual consumption patterns, and opportunities for improved operational planning. Review maintenance and equipment performance records to assess their impact on plant efficiency and energy consumption. Support energy audits through remote document reviews, data analysis, technical assessments, and follow-up recommendations. Establish performance monitoring procedures, reporting standards, and energy efficiency benchmarks. Evaluate proposed equipment upgrades and control strategy changes from an energy performance and lifecycle cost perspective. Provide technical guidance to engineering and operations teams on district cooling efficiency, performance indicators, and energy management practices. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Building Services Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. Significant experience in district cooling systems, central cooling plants, HVAC engineering, energy management, or thermal system optimization. Strong understanding of chilled water production, distribution networks, thermal energy transfer, and district cooling plant operations. Practical knowledge of centrifugal, screw, or other industrial chiller technologies. Experience analyzing plant performance indicators, including COP, kW/RT, cooling capacity, flow rates, and temperature differentials. Understanding of cooling tower performance, condenser water systems, chilled water pumping, and heat exchanger operation. Experience with energy modeling, operational benchmarking, load analysis, and efficiency improvement assessments. Familiarity with BMS, SCADA, energy management systems, and remote monitoring platforms. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and technical reporting tools; experience with Power BI or other analytics platforms is an advantage. Knowledge of hydraulic system principles, pump curves, control valves, differential pressure management, and variable-speed operation. Understanding of thermal energy metering, energy consumption measurement, and data quality validation. Ability to interpret mechanical schematics, system diagrams, equipment specifications, and operational performance reports. Experience conducting technical evaluations and developing evidence-based energy optimization recommendations. Knowledge of energy efficiency standards, sustainability principles, and relevant HVAC engineering practices. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly when working with large volumes of operational data. Excellent technical writing and communication skills. Ability to coordinate effectively with geographically distributed engineering and operations teams. Professional engineering credentials or relevant energy management certifications are an advantage. What We Offer A fully remote, work-from-home opportunity based in the UAE. The opportunity to support energy efficiency and operational improvements in large-scale district cooling infrastructure. Exposure to advanced cooling technologies, performance analytics, and energy optimization systems. A collaborative environment involving engineering, operations, and sustainability professionals. Opportunities for professional development in thermal systems, energy management, and district cooling optimization. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit an updated CV highlighting their experience in district cooling, HVAC performance analysis, energy optimization, and relevant monitoring technologies. Application Subject: Application – Senior District Cooling Energy Optimization Specialist (UAE Remote) Candidates should confirm applicable employment arrangements, residency requirements, and work authorization before accepting an offer. Remote-work scope: This position is focused on remote engineering analysis, operational data review, performance monitoring, energy modeling, technical reporting, and virtual coordination. Physical plant inspections, equipment testing, maintenance, mechanical adjustments, control panel interventions, and on-site commissioning must be performed by appropriately qualified local personnel. Any engineering certifications, statutory inspections, safety approvals, or formal technical sign-offs must be completed by professionals holding the required local authorization.
